binders: m, n, and q are arbitrary natural numbers, with no positivity assumptions.
theta, gmin, and Gmin are arbitrary real numbers.
A is an arbitrary real matrix indexed by Fin m × Fin n, hence of dimensions m by n.
B is an arbitrary real matrix indexed by Fin n × Fin q, hence of dimensions n by q.
conclusions: 4·(n:Real)^2·(theta⁻¹)^2·Gmin·N(A)·N(B) ≤ 4·(n:Real)^2·theta⁻¹·gmin·N(A)·N(B), where N is the maximum row-sum norm defined below.
mathematical_definitions: For an r-by-s real matrix X, N(X) is the real coercion of sup_{i in Fin r} sum_{j in Fin s} nnnorm(X(i,j)), where the sum and supremum are first taken in the nonnegative reals.
Equivalently under the standard real norm, N(X) = max_{i in Fin r} sum_{j in Fin s} |X(i,j)|, with the maximum over an empty row-index set defined to be 0.
Thus N(A) uses rows Fin m and columns Fin n, while N(B) uses rows Fin n and columns Fin q.
(n:Real)^2 is the square of the natural dimension n after casting it to Real; theta⁻¹ is real inversion; the coefficient is exactly the real number 4.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every choice of natural dimensions m, n, q, real parameters theta, gmin, Gmin, an m-by-n real matrix A, and an n-by-q real matrix B, if theta is at least 1 and 0 ≤ Gmin ≤ gmin, then 4 times n squared times the square of the reciprocal of theta times Gmin times the maximum absolute row-sum norms of A and B is at most 4 times n squared times the reciprocal of theta times gmin times those same two matrix norms.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimensions m, n, and q may be zero; no nonempty-index assumption is present.

If m = 0, then N(A) = 0. If q = 0, then N(B) = 0. If n = 0, the explicit factor (n:Real)^2 is 0 and the relevant row sums are also degenerate. In all such cases the conclusion can collapse to a trivial inequality.
The conclusion is also trivial when either matrix norm is zero; no nonzero-matrix assumption is present.
The hypotheses imply theta > 0 and gmin ≥ 0, although only 1 ≤ theta, 0 ≤ Gmin, and Gmin ≤ gmin are explicitly encoded.
Gmin may equal 0, and neither scalar comparison is strict.
A and B are used only through their separate maximum row-sum norms. The proposition does not mention the matrix product A·B or any entrywise relationship between the matrices.
There are no existential witnesses, approximation quantities, error terms, algorithms, equality claims, or optimality claims encoded in the proposition.
ambiguities: The packet gives Nat.AtLeastTwo only as an inductive predicate Nat → Prop and omits its constructors, so its exact internal logical characterization cannot be recovered from the supplied declaration alone. This does not make the coefficient ambiguous: D004 supplies the required witness for 3+1, and D026 interprets the resulting numeral as its natural cast, namely the real number 4.
